title: Many resist and perish by their own fault
source_text: XLVI. Fatentur multos, quos Deus eo modo vocat ad fidem & conversionem, nolle Deum vocantem sequi, & Spiritui Sancto quae ad salutem eorum faciunt suggerenti resistere, ac tandem motus illos per verbum & Spiritum Sanctum in iis excitatos penitus extinguere, & sic propria culpa in aeternum perire.
pass_a_gloss: XLVI. They confess that many, whom God calls in that way to faith & conversion, will not follow God calling, & resist the Holy Spirit suggesting the things which make for their salvation, and at last wholly extinguish those motions excited in them through the word & the Holy Spirit, & so perish eternally by their own fault.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVI. They admit that many whom God calls to faith and conversion in this way refuse to follow God's call, resist the Holy Spirit as he prompts them toward what makes for their salvation, and in the end entirely stifle the motions that the word and the Holy Spirit stirred in them, and so are lost for ever through their own fault.

lemmas.latin: quae ad salutem eorum faciunt suggerenti
lemmas.gloss: suggesting the things which make for their salvation
perish eternally by their own fault

choices.english: things preliminary to conversion or regeneration
choices.why: The British delegates' term for inward effects that go before regeneration and can be stifled.
